after_fields.mode_of_action_notes: CURATOR: 26-membered macrocyclic thiopeptide antibiotic isolated from the marine actinomycete Nocardiopsis sp. TFS65-07 that inhibits Gram-positive bacterial protein biosynthesis by targeting the 50S ribosomal subunit (Engelhardt et al. 2010, DOI:10.1128/AEM.00741-10, PMID:20562278; Engelhardt et al. 2010, DOI:10.1128/AEM.01442-10, PMID:20851988).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: TP-1161 is a 26-membered series d1 thiopeptide antibiotic isolated from marine Nocardiopsis sp. TFS65-07 (BGC0000615) with potent activity against Gram-positive bacteria including Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Enterococcus faecalis via 50S ribosomal subunit translation inhibition (Engelhardt et al. 2010, DOI:10.1128/AEM.00741-10, PMID:20562278; Engelhardt et al. 2010, DOI:10.1128/AEM.01442-10, PMID:20851988).

evidence.notes: Engelhardt et al. 2010 (Appl Environ Microbiol 76:4969-4976; DOI:10.1128/AEM.00741-10) isolated TP-1161, determined its 26-membered thiopeptide structure, and characterized its Gram-positive antibacterial activity (MIC 0.25-1 ug/mL).
Engelhardt et al. 2010 (Appl Environ Microbiol 76:7093-7101; DOI:10.1128/AEM.01442-10) characterized the TP-1161 ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC0000615) in Nocardiopsis sp. TFS65-07.

added_history_event.changes: Populated PROTEIN_SYNTHESIS_INHIBITION (MICROBIAL_TARGET) mode_of_action, and primary-literature bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit molecular_targets on TP-1161 backed by Engelhardt et al. 2010 (PMID:20562278, PMID:20851988; issue #1360).

after_fields.mode_of_action_notes: CURATOR: (5S)-Clavam natural product produced by Streptomyces clavuligerus and Streptomyces antibioticus that lacks beta-lactamase inhibitory activity due to its (5S) ring-junction stereochemistry and acts as an antifungal antimetabolite inhibiting fungal cellular metabolic pathways (Brown et al. 1979, DOI:10.1039/C39790000282; Jensen et al. 2000, DOI:10.1128/AAC.44.3.720-726.2000, PMID:10681345; Tahlan et al. 2007, DOI:10.1016/j.chembiol.2006.11.012, PMID:17317567).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Whole-cell antifungal bioassays and (5S)-clavam biosynthetic pathway studies demonstrate that 2-formyloxymethylclavam inhibits fungal growth without inhibiting bacterial beta-lactamases (Brown et al. 1979, DOI:10.1039/C39790000282; Jensen et al. 2000, DOI:10.1128/AAC.44.3.720-726.2000, PMID:10681345; Tahlan et al. 2007, DOI:10.1016/j.chembiol.2006.11.012, PMID:17317567).

evidence.notes: Jensen et al. 2000 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 44:720-726; DOI:10.1128/AAC.44.3.720-726.2000) characterized the paralogous early biosynthetic steps for clavulanic acid and the antifungal (5S)-clavam metabolites including 2-formyloxymethylclavam in Streptomyces clavuligerus.
Tahlan et al. 2007 (Chem Biol 14:131-142; DOI:10.1016/j.chembiol.2006.11.012) established the late (5S)-clavam biosynthetic pathway and antifungal bioactivity of 2-formyloxymethylclavam.
Brown et al. 1979 (J Chem Soc Chem Commun 1979:282-283) isolated 2-formyloxymethylclavam from Streptomyces clavuligerus and reported its antifungal activity and absence of beta-lactamase inhibition.

added_history_event.changes: Populated OTHER (MICROBIAL_TARGET) mode_of_action, and primary-literature fungal cellular metabolic process molecular_targets on 2-formyloxymethylclavam (PMID:10681345, PMID:17317567, DOI:10.1039/C39790000282; issue #1360).

after_fields.mode_of_action_notes: CURATOR: Semisynthetic spiropiperidyl rifamycin antibiotic that binds the conserved rifamycin pocket on the beta subunit (RpoB) of bacterial DNA-directed RNA polymerase and inhibits transcription initiation and nascent RNA elongation (Artsimovitch et al. 2005, DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2005.07.014, PMID:16096056, PDB:2A68; Floss & Yu 2005, DOI:10.1021/cr030112j, PMID:15700959).

before_molecular_targets.target_label: rifamycin sensitive beta-subunit of RNA polymerase (rpoB)
before_molecular_targets.experimental_context: CARD/ARO database assertion; target organism, strain, and assay are not specified. RpoB is asserted as a target in the RNA polymerase complex.

evidence.notes: CARD/ARO asserts targeted_by_antibiotic ARO:3000530 (rifabutin); database assertion, not a primary citation.

after_molecular_targets.target_label: rifamycin sensitive beta-subunit of RNA polymerase (rpoB)
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: CARD/ARO database assertion; target organism, strain, and assay are not specified. RpoB is asserted as a target in the RNA polymerase complex.

evidence.notes: CARD/ARO asserts targeted_by_antibiotic ARO:3000530 (rifabutin); database assertion, not a primary citation.

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: X-ray crystal structure of Thermus thermophilus RNA polymerase holoenzyme bound to rifabutin at 2.5 A resolution (PDB:2A68) and biochemical transcription assays with Escherichia coli RNA polymerase show rifabutin binding the RpoB beta-subunit pocket and blocking synthesis of nascent RNA transcripts beyond 2 nucleotides (Artsimovitch et al. 2005, DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2005.07.014, PMID:16096056; Floss & Yu 2005, DOI:10.1021/cr030112j, PMID:15700959).

evidence.notes: Artsimovitch et al. 2005 (Cell 122:351-363; DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2005.07.014) determined the 2.5 A crystal structure of Thermus thermophilus RNA polymerase in complex with rifabutin (PDB:2A68) and measured direct transcription inhibition on Escherichia coli RNA polymerase.

Floss & Yu 2005 (Chem Rev 105:621-632; DOI:10.1021/cr030112j) reviewed rifamycin structure-activity relationships, bacterial RNA polymerase RpoB binding, and mycobacterial RpoB resistance mutations for rifabutin.

added_history_event.changes: Added SEMISYNTHETIC biosynthesis_origin, curator-verified NUCLEIC_ACID_SYNTHESIS_INHIBITION (MICROBIAL_TARGET) mode_of_action, and primary-literature DNA-directed RNA polymerase complex molecular_targets on rifabutin (PMID:16096056, PMID:15700959; issue #1361).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Rifaximin binds the beta subunit (RpoB) of bacterial DNA-directed RNA polymerase (including Escherichia coli RNAP) to block transcription initiation and bacterial RNA synthesis without inhibiting mammalian RNA polymerase (Gillis & Brogden 1995, DOI:10.2165/00003495-199549030-00009, PMID:7774516; Jiang & DuPont 2005, DOI:10.1159/000081991, PMID:15855749; Floss & Yu 2005, DOI:10.1021/cr030112j, PMID:15700959).

evidence.notes: Gillis & Brogden 1995 (Drugs 49:467-484; DOI:10.2165/00003495-199549030-00009) characterized rifaximin binding to the beta subunit (RpoB) of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase and inhibition of bacterial RNA synthesis.

Jiang & DuPont 2005 (Chemotherapy 51 Suppl 1:67-72; DOI:10.1159/000081991) reviewed the mechanism of action of rifaximin via bacterial RNA polymerase RpoB binding and enteropathogenic Escherichia coli susceptibility.
Floss & Yu 2005 (Chem Rev 105:621-632; DOI:10.1021/cr030112j) characterized the conserved rifamycin mode of action on bacterial DNA-directed RNA polymerase beta subunit RpoB.

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: X-ray crystal structures of Escherichia coli EF-Tu-GDP-GE2270A at 2.35 A resolution (Heffron & Jurnak 2000, DOI:10.1021/bi9913597, PMID:10625477, PDB:1D8T) and Thermus thermophilus EF-Tu-GppNHp-GE2270A at 1.6 A resolution (Parmeggiani et al. 2006, DOI:10.1021/bi0525122, PMID:16734421, PDB:2C77) establish that GE2270A binds the 3'-aminoacyl-tRNA pocket on domain 2 of EF-Tu and prevents aminoacyl-tRNA binding.

evidence.notes: Heffron & Jurnak 2000 (Biochemistry 39:37-45; DOI:10.1021/bi9913597) resolved the 2.35 A cocrystal structure of Escherichia coli EF-Tu-GDP bound to GE2270A (PDB:1D8T), showing steric occlusion of the aminoacyl-tRNA binding cleft on domain 2.

Parmeggiani et al. 2006 (Biochemistry 45:6846-6857; DOI:10.1021/bi0525122) resolved the 1.6 A cocrystal structure of Thermus thermophilus EF-Tu in complex with GE2270A (PDB:2C77) and characterized E. coli EF-Tu resistance substitutions.
